mainEntity.name: What is considered a guest apartment on a residential property?

acceptedAnswer.text: A guest apartment—often referred to as an accessory dwelling unit (ADU), in-law suite, or carriage house—is a self-contained living space on a residential property that includes dedicated sleeping, bathroom, and often basic kitchen facilities. It can be built as a detached backyard cottage, an addition attached to the primary home, or a conversion of an existing space like a garage. Unlike a simple guest bedroom, an apartment gives visitors or extended family private living quarters. The exact scope depends on whether the unit serves short-term guests, aging parents, or adult children, as layout priorities shift based on accessibility and long-term independence.
acceptedAnswer.description: A guest apartment is a self-contained living area with a sleeping space, bathroom, and often kitchen facilities, built as an addition, detached unit, or conversion on a residential property.
